title: Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act)
text:
Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act) - 1. Section 80C — Investment & Savings Deductions:
- **Maximum Limit:** **₹1,50,000** per financial year across all eligible instruments.
- **Eligible Investments & Expenses:**
  - Employee Provident Fund (EPF) 12% deduction and Voluntary Provident Fund (VPF).
  - Public Provident Fund (PPF) — 15 year government backed scheme.
  - Equity Linked Savings Scheme (ELSS) mutual funds (3-year lock-in).
  - Life Insurance Premiums (for self, spouse, and children).
  - National Savings Certificate (NSC), 5-Year Bank Fixed Deposits (tax-saver).
  - Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY) for girl child.
  - Principal repayment on housing loan for purchase/construction of residential house property.
  - Tuition fees paid for full-time education of up to 2 children in Indian schools/universities.
  - Stamp duty and registration charges paid during house property purchase.

---

title: Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act)
text:
Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act) - 2. Section 80D — Health & Medical Insurance Premiums:
- **Self, Spouse, and Dependent Children:**
  - Regular individuals: Up to **₹25,000**.
  - If self or spouse is a Senior Citizen (60+ years): Up to **₹50,000**.
- **Parents:**
  - Non-senior parents: Additional up to **₹25,000**.
  - Senior citizen parents (60+ years): Additional up to **₹50,000**.
- **Preventive Health Checkup:** Up to **₹5,000** within the overall limit.
- **Maximum Combined Deduction:** Up to **₹1,00,000** (when both self/spouse and parents are senior citizens).

---

title: Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act)
text:
Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act) - 3. Section 24(b) — Home Loan Interest Deduction:
- **Self-Occupied Property:** Deduction of interest paid on housing loan up to **₹2,00,000** per financial year.
- **Let-Out Property:** Full interest deductible against rental income, but loss under house property that can be set off against salary is capped at **₹2,00,000**.

---

title: Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act)
text:
Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act) - 4. Section 80CCD(1B) — National Pension Scheme (NPS):
- **Additional Deduction:** Up to **₹50,000** for voluntary employee contributions to NPS Tier-1 account.
- This is **over and above** the ₹1,50,000 limit under Section 80C, allowing an aggregate ₹2,00,000 deduction.

---

title: Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act)
text:
Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act) - 5. Section 10(13A) — House Rent Allowance (HRA) Exemption:
Exempt portion of HRA is the **least of the following three amounts**:
1. **Actual HRA received** from employer during the period.
2. **Rent paid minus 10% of Salary** (Salary = Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance).
3. **50% of Salary** for accommodation situated in Metro cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai) OR **40% of Salary** for Non-Metro cities (Pune, Bangalore, Hyderabad, etc.).


- If annual rent paid exceeds **₹1,00,000**, employee must mandatorily furnish **Landlord PAN**.
- Rent receipts and rental agreement must be submitted for HR verification.

---

title: Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act)
text:
Chapter VI-A Deductions & Section 10 Exemptions (Income Tax Act) - 6. Section 80E & Section 80G:
- **Section 80E:** Full interest paid on loan taken for higher education of self, spouse, or children (deductible for up to 8 continuous assessment years).
- **Section 80G:** Donations to specified charitable funds and relief institutions (50% or 100% deduction depending on qualifying fund status).

title: Organization Leave Policy, Gratuity & Statutory FAQs
text:
Organization Leave Policy, Gratuity & Statutory FAQs - 1. Annual Leave Entitlement (FY 2025–26):
Every confirmed staff member is entitled to the following leave quotas per financial year:

1. **Casual Leave (CL):**
   - **Quota:** 12 days per year (credited 1 day at the start of each month).
   - **Lapse Policy:** Cannot be carried forward to next financial year; lapses on March 31st.
   - **Maximum Continuous Leave:** 3 days at a time without prior approval.

2. **Sick / Medical Leave (SL):**
   - **Quota:** 10 days per year on full pay.
   - **Medical Certificate:** Required from a Registered Medical Practitioner for illness exceeding 2 consecutive working days.

3. **Earned / Privilege Leave (EL):**
   - **Quota:** 20 days per year (accrued at 1.66 days per month of active service).
   - **Carry-over & Encashment:** Can be accumulated up to a maximum of **300 days**.
   - **Encashment at Retirement/Separation:** Tax-exempt up to **₹25,00,000** under Section 10(10AA) for non-government employees.

---

title: Organization Leave Policy, Gratuity & Statutory FAQs
text:
Organization Leave Policy, Gratuity & Statutory FAQs - 2. Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972:
An employee is eligible for statutory gratuity upon completion of at least **5 continuous years of service** with the organization (or upon death/disablement without minimum tenure).


$$\text{Gratuity Amount} = \frac{15 \times \text{Last Drawn (Basic + DA)} \times \text{Years of Service}}{26}$$

- **Working Days in Month:** Fixed by law at **26 days**.
- **Fraction of Year:** If months in the final fraction exceed 6 months, it is rounded up to 1 full completed year.
- **Maximum Tax-Exempt Gratuity:** Up to **₹20,00,000** under Section 10(10) of the Income Tax Act.

---

title: Organization Leave Policy, Gratuity & Statutory FAQs
text:
Organization Leave Policy, Gratuity & Statutory FAQs - 3. Loss of Pay (LOP) & Arrears Computation:
- **Daily Wage Rate:** Computed as $\frac{\text{Monthly Gross Earnings}}{\text{Days in Month}}$.
- **LOP Deduction:** $\text{Daily Rate} \times \text{Unpaid Days}$.
- **Salary Arrears:** Calculated when DA revision or pay increment is implemented with retrospective effective dates.

title: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO)
text:
Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO) - 1. Statutory Applicability & Wage Ceiling:
- **Establishment Coverage:** Mandatory for every establishment employing 20 or more persons.
- **Statutory Wage Ceiling:** **₹15,000 per month** (Basic + Dearness Allowance + Retaining Allowance).
- **Statutory Cap on PF Calculation:**
  - If gross basic wage > ₹15,000, employer may opt to cap employee PF contribution at ₹1,800/month (12% of ₹15,000) OR compute 12% on actual Basic + DA.
  - PaySoft standard configuration computes 12% of Basic up to the ₹1,800 threshold or statutory actuals.

---

title: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO)
text:
Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO) - 2. Contribution Breakdown & Split:
Total EPF contribution is split into Employee Share and Employer Share:

| Component | Share | Rate (%) | Wage Base | Maximum Cap / Month |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Employee Share** | Employee | **12.00%** | Basic + DA | ₹1,800 (if capped) |
| **Employer EPF Share** | Employer | **3.67%** | Basic + DA | ₹550 (if wage = ₹15k) |
| **Employer EPS Share** | Employer (Pension) | **8.33%** | Capped at ₹15,000 | **₹1,250** maximum |
| **EDLI Contribution** | Employer (Insurance) | **0.50%** | Capped at ₹15,000 | ₹75 maximum |
| **EPF Admin Charges** | Employer | **0.50%** | Gross EPF Wages | Minimum ₹500/month |


- Employee pays: **12%** (All to EPF Account 1).
- Employer pays: **12%** (3.67% to EPF Account 1 + 8.33% to EPS Account 10).
- Total statutory deposit in EPFO: **24%** + admin charges.

---

title: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO)
text:
Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO) - 3. Universal Account Number (UAN) & Statutory Forms:
- **UAN (Universal Account Number):** 12-digit permanent number assigned to every PF member.
- **Form 11 (EPF Declaration Form):** Filled by newly joined employee declaring previous PF account and Aadhaar/PAN linking.
- **Form 19:** Final PF settlement application upon leaving service.
- **Form 10C:** Scheme Certificate / EPS Pension withdrawal application.
- **Form 31:** Application for advance / partial withdrawal from EPF (for house purchase, medical illness, marriage, education).

---

title: Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO)
text:
Employees' Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (EPFO) - 4. ECR (Electronic Challan-cum-Return) Version 2 Format:
EPFO requires employers to file monthly returns in `#~#` delimited format:
- Field 1: UAN (12 chars)
- Field 2: Member Name (30 chars)
- Field 3: Gross Wages
- Field 4: EPF Wages (capped at 15,000)
- Field 5: EPS Wages (capped at 15,000)
- Field 6: EDLI Wages (capped at 15,000)
- Field 7: EE Share (12% of EPF Wages)
- Field 8: EPS Share (8.33% of EPS Wages, max 1250)
- Field 9: ER Share (EE Share minus EPS Share)
- Field 10: NCP (Non-Contributory Period) Days
- Field 11: Refund of Advances

title: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC)
text:
Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC) - 1. Statutory Wage Threshold & Applicability:
- **Applicability:** Factories and commercial establishments employing 10 or more persons in notified areas.
- **Gross Monthly Wage Ceiling:** **₹21,000 per month**.
- **Employees with Disabilities:** Gross wage ceiling is **₹25,000 per month**.
- **Wage definition for ESI:** Basic, DA, HRA, City Compensatory Allowance, Special Allowances, and attendance bonus (excludes annual bonus, gratuity, and retrenchment compensation).

---

title: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC)
text:
Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC) - 2. Contribution Rates:
Effective from revised Ministry of Labour rates:

| Contributor | Statutory Rate (%) | Calculation Base |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Employee Contribution (IP)** | **0.75%** | Gross Monthly Wages |
| **Employer Contribution** | **3.25%** | Gross Monthly Wages |
| **Total Contribution** | **4.00%** | Deposited with ESIC |

- **Exempt Employees:** Employees whose daily average wage is up to ₹176 are exempt from paying employee's share, but employer must pay full 3.25%.

---

title: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC)
text:
Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC) - 3. Statutory Benefits for Insured Persons (IP):
- **Medical Benefit:** Full medical care for self and dependent family members from day one of insurable employment.
- **Sickness Benefit:** Cash benefit at 70% of average daily wage for up to 91 days in two consecutive benefit periods.
- **Maternity Benefit:** 100% of average daily wage for 26 weeks for confinement and 6 weeks for miscarriage.
- **Disablement Benefit:** 90% of wage for temporary or permanent disablement arising out of employment injury.
- **Dependents' Benefit:** Monthly pension to dependents in case of employment injury resulting in death.

---

title: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC)
text:
Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (ESIC) - 4. Compliance Deadlines & Records:
- **Monthly Contribution Filing:** Payment and return must be filed online via ESIC Portal on or before the **15th of the following month**.
- **Contribution Periods:**
  - 1st April to 30th September (corresponding cash benefit period: 1st January to 30th June).
  - 1st October to 31st March (corresponding cash benefit period: 1st July to 31st December).

title: Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27)
text:
Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) - 1. Overview of Income Tax Regimes:
In India, salaried employees can choose between two tax regimes for each financial year:
1. **New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC):** Default tax regime with lower slab rates and higher tax-free threshold, but disallowing most Chapter VI-A itemized exemptions/deductions (except standard deduction, employer NPS under 80CCD(2), and employer PF contribution).
2. **Old Tax Regime:** Traditional tax regime with higher slab rates, but allowing all Chapter VI-A deductions (80C, 80D, 80CCD(1B), 80E, 80G), Section 10 exemptions (HRA, LTA), and Section 24(b) home loan interest.

---

title: Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27)
text:
Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) - 2. New Tax Regime Slabs (FY 2025–26 / AY 2026–27):
Under Union Budget revisions effective for FY 2025–26:

| Total Taxable Income Slab (₹) | Income Tax Rate |
| :--- | :--- |
| Up to ₹3,00,000 | Nil (0%) |
| ₹3,00,001 to ₹7,00,000 | 5% |
| ₹7,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 | 10% |
| ₹10,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 | 15% |
| ₹12,00,001 to ₹15,00,000 | 20% |
| Above ₹15,00,000 | 30% |


- **Standard Deduction:** Increased to **₹75,000** for salaried employees and pensioners.
- **Section 87A Tax Rebate:** Tax rebate is available for taxable income up to **₹7,00,000**. Tax rebate amount is up to ₹25,000, meaning tax payable becomes ₹0.
- **Effective Tax-Free Salary:** With the ₹75,000 standard deduction + ₹7,00,000 rebate threshold, any employee with gross annual salary up to **₹7,75,000 pays ZERO income tax**.
- **Family Pension Deduction:** Increased from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000.

---

title: Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27)
text:
Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) - 3. Old Tax Regime Slabs (FY 2025–26 / AY 2026–27):
For individuals below 60 years of age:

| Total Taxable Income Slab (₹) | Income Tax Rate |
| :--- | :--- |
| Up to ₹2,50,000 | Nil (0%) |
| ₹2,50,001 to ₹5,00,000 | 5% |
| ₹5,00,001 to ₹10,00,000 | 20% |
| Above ₹10,00,000 | 30% |

- **Senior Citizens (60 to 79 years):** Basic exemption is ₹3,00,000.
- **Super Senior Citizens (80+ years):** Basic exemption is ₹5,00,000.
- **Standard Deduction:** Fixed at **₹50,000**.
- **Section 87A Rebate:** Applicable only if total taxable income is up to **₹5,00,000** (max rebate ₹12,500).

---

title: Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27)
text:
Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) - 4. Health & Education Cess and Surcharge:
- **Health and Education Cess:** **4%** applied on the sum of income tax and surcharge.
- **Surcharge on High Net Worth Individuals:**
  - Income ₹50 Lakhs to ₹1 Crore: **10%**
  - Income ₹1 Crore to ₹2 Crores: **15%**
  - Income ₹2 Crores to ₹5 Crores: **25%**
  - Under New Tax Regime, the maximum surcharge rate is capped at **25%** (whereas Old Regime had a 37% slab for > ₹5 Cr).

---

title: Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27)
section: 5. Which Regime Should an Employee Choose?
text:
Indian Income Tax Rules & Slabs — FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27) - 5. Which Regime Should an Employee Choose?:
- **Breakeven Point:** For an annual salary of ₹12,00,000 to ₹15,00,000, if an employee's total eligible deductions (80C + 80D + HRA + Home Loan Interest) exceed **₹3,75,000 to ₹4,25,000**, the Old Regime is generally beneficial.
- If total deductions are less than ₹3,50,000, the **New Regime** yields higher take-home pay with lower tax liability and no requirement to lock funds in tax-saving instruments.

title: State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India
text:
State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India - Section 1:
Under Article 276(2) of the Indian Constitution, the maximum Professional Tax that can be levied on any person is capped at **₹2,500 per year**.

---

title: State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India
text:
State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India - 1. Maharashtra (State Code: MH):
Under the Maharashtra State Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1975 (with latest gender-neutral / women exemption amendments):


| Monthly Gross Salary (₹) | Monthly PTax (₹) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Up to ₹7,500 | Nil (₹0) |
| ₹7,501 to ₹10,000 | ₹175 per month |
| Above ₹10,000 | **₹200 per month** (₹300 in February) |


| Monthly Gross Salary (₹) | Monthly PTax (₹) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Up to ₹25,000 | **Nil (Exempt)** |
| Above ₹25,000 | **₹200 per month** (₹300 in February) |

*Note: Total annual tax = 11 months × ₹200 + 1 month (Feb) × ₹300 = **₹2,500**.*

---

title: State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India
text:
State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India - 4. Tamil Nadu (State Code: TN):

title: State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India
text:
State-wise Professional Tax (PTax) Slabs in India - 5. Other States & Exemptions:
- **Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh:** No Professional Tax is currently levied.
- **Telangana / Andhra Pradesh:** Monthly slabs from ₹150 to ₹200 (for salary > ₹20,000).
- **Gujarat:** Gross up to ₹12,000: Nil; > ₹12,000: ₹200/month.
